cells.tense: You're here, and the practice is in your hands right now.
cells.verb: keep working the same thing pass after pass until it goes deep
cells.place: in the place where you step back and take in the whole shape of what's in front of you
cells.ask: Pick one piece of what you already see and sharpen it finer than anyone asked for — on your own, for no reason but the sharpening. The seeing gets clearer, and the work stays yours.
cells.core:
You see the whole of it because you've worked every part of it. This isn't a flash of insight — it's what long practice turns into, the kind of sight that comes from going back to the bench until the thing stops surprising you. You're not above the work looking down; you're inside it and can still read the whole shape. That's hard-won, and it's working.

What it's free to feed now is finer distinction. Take one thing you can already see and go one pass deeper — alone, unhurried, not for anyone. The practice doesn't need pushing; it just keeps sharpening what you can tell apart.
cells.sheetLine: You see the whole shape because you've worked every part of it.

cells.tense: You're bracing for a finished picture that keeps not arriving.
cells.verb: keep working the same thing pass after pass until it goes deep
cells.place: in the place where you step back and take in the whole shape of what's in front of you
cells.ask: Bring what you've built so far to people who'd enjoy it, and let it be glad and unfinished in their company. The parts that never belonged fall away on their own once you stop guarding the whole.
cells.core:
You're refining your read of the whole thing past the point where refining helps. Every pass finds another corner that isn't quite right yet, and somewhere ahead is the version where it finally all holds together — so you keep working, and the picture keeps receding. The grind has become the point, and the seeing it was for has gone tight.

The way back isn't another pass. It's taking what you've got out of the workshop and into a room with people who'd be glad to see it — not for critique, for the pleasure of it. Shared like that, the thing you keep bracing for stops mattering, and what doesn't belong drops without you having to cut it.
cells.sheetLine: You're polishing the whole picture instead of living in it.

cells.tense: You're still standing at a door you already walked past.
cells.verb: keep working the same thing pass after pass until it goes deep
cells.place: in the place where you step back and take in the whole shape of what's in front of you
cells.ask: Say one pattern you see out loud, to one person, as a plain fact — lay it out clearly enough that it holds. Naming it pulls you back to the bench, and what was holding you back comes down on its own.
cells.core:
You used to see the whole thing because you kept at it, and somewhere behind you, you stopped keeping at it. The sight is still there in outline — you can tell when something's off — but it's getting fainter, because it was built from practice and the practice has lapsed. You're not wrong about what you see. You're just not standing where you'd see it clearly anymore.

Forcing yourself back to the work isn't the way in. Instead, take one pattern you already notice and state it plainly to someone — not as a hunch, as the way things are. Laying it out so it holds is what draws the current back through the part of you that stopped showing up.
cells.sheetLine: The sight came from the work, and you've left the work.

cells.tense: Pen down, in a room you're already writing in.
cells.verb: keep working the same thing pass after pass until it goes deep
cells.place: in the place where you step back and take in the whole shape of what's in front of you
cells.ask: Notice what you move toward before you've decided to, and say "I built that" about one thing you've been calling a knack. The seeing comes home to the one who earned it.
cells.core:
You already read the whole shape of a situation faster and truer than most people around you — and you call it luck, or a hunch, or just noticing. It isn't. It's what going back to the same thing until it stopped surprising you turns into. The craft is running. You just haven't signed your name to it.

The way back is simpler than it sounds. Watch where you move when you're not deciding — what your hands reach for, what you turn toward without thinking. That pull is the practice speaking. Follow it on purpose once, and call the result yours, and the sight starts answering to the person who built it.
cells.sheetLine: You've already earned the sight. You keep calling it a hunch.

flags.detail: "for years" — a cell knows no one's past
